Requirements: Node.js >= 22.12.0 and pnpm >= 11.18.0. Root package.json, package manifests and pnpm-lock.yaml define the actual commands and dependency versions.

pnpm install
pnpm dev:desktop
# Web development
pnpm dev:web
# Public packages and Web; excludes Desktop
pnpm build
# Desktop frontend, main process and preload
pnpm build:desktop
# Validated installer; macOS defaults to DMG, add --with-zip for ZIP
pnpm package:desktop
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test

Workspace navigation uses Home, Search and All content, with Charts available as an All content tab. Cmd/Ctrl+P opens a cancellable quick file picker. Settings combines personal and workspace preferences in a bounded dialog; text and numeric drafts save when editing finishes. The workspace name opens the switcher, with creation separated from filtering.

Documents offer slash insertion, paragraph actions, stable block links and live read-only excerpts. Native templates cover technical proposals, ADRs, system design and requirements. Content management adds portable properties, saved filters, persistent checkpoints, conflict comparison, independent recovery copies and managed images. Folder/ZIP migration preserves linked notes and assets; portable archives include native sources, Markdown and conversion reports.

Standalone documents add nested-list folding, details, inline/block LaTeX, binary attachments, local media and PDF reading with stable page links. HTTPS embeds are click-to-load and retain external navigation. Portable v2 preserves original resources; task lists, databases and clipping are deferred.
Agent integration and independent content updates

Workspaces expose AGENTS.md, portable project configuration and a shared verd CLI for AI authoring. System introduction and the Document authoring recommendations ship with Desktop and share the product version. In the workspace switcher, choose Open system introduction. An update marker appears inside the corresponding workspace when the bundled content differs from the installed copy. Backups are optional; choosing a backup folder creates a copy in the normal workspace list. See the development and desktop guides for details.

Version context: application, SDK, UI and Agent packages are prepared as 2.1.0 for this explicitly authorized early-stage release. Breaking API changes remain documented and require migration from historical 2.0 consumers. Future releases follow the existing version rules. Local artifacts do not establish registry publication. Agent defaults are maintained in packages/product/agent-patterns/agent/; user recommendations have an independent source.

Settings → Skills edits common workspace instructions and pattern supplements as standard .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md files, with YAML metadata and Markdown bodies. Default patterns and native validation continue to apply. verd context lists workspaceSkills for agents to read on demand; Skill changes invalidate pending plans. File-version conflicts preserve drafts, and bundled workspace updates preserve user Skills and referenced resources.
Independent custom Skills and default Skill viewing

Settings → Custom Skills provides creation, editing and recycling of independently named workspace Skills. Standard SKILL.md files under .agents/skills are discovered automatically. Names are fixed after creation; descriptions and Markdown bodies remain editable, while optional metadata and reference resources are preserved. Custom Skills have no pattern association and agents activate them only when their descriptions match the task.

The Prompts page offers View default Skill beside the scope selector. The read-only viewer shows the common authoring Skill, the selected pattern Skill and its native rule document, with full Markdown source available. Default Skill entrances and the common authoring Skill are maintained in the content package; rules and templates retain their native source. The shared authoring path remains compatible.

Native JSON exports with managed images or attachments use verd-canvas-bundle v2, carrying the file closure and original resource bytes. Import validates hashes and commits files and resources together; native/v1 input remains supported. Web exposes virtual workspace creation and history, while Desktop additionally provides directory selection, system introduction and the Document authoring recommendations. Saved workspace names remain consistent with history and search.

Regression verification covers unit tests, Web and Desktop development and production builds, real package consumers and fresh Agent resources. Doctor exits 0 when ready and 1 when unready without initializing the project.

Ordinary resources appear at their real paths and open in a read-only preview or the system application (download on Web). Project data, assets, history and cache live under the excluded .verdscrolls/ directory. Every diagram is an independent source file, shown once in the directory tree; canvases share it through stable references. Existing resource stores migrate without rewriting attachment addresses.

Workspace versions use a root Git repository. Commit one complete file or all workspace changes, preview content and dependencies from the same commit, and restore one file or the workspace. Editing still saves automatically, while recovery snapshots and automatic commits are disabled.

Desktop and the local Web service use system Git and existing credentials for manual remote synchronization. Diverged histories require an external Git tool. The standalone IndexedDB SDK host provides local Git history in the browser. Legacy snapshots remain readable and restorable. Permanent deletion reviews a history rewrite plan and reports local cleanup, remote reference updates and pending provider cleanup separately.

File and directory menus provide Version history with explicit creation, preview and restore. Workspace settings → Version management contains workspace history and storage configuration. Git is the current adapter behind a provider-independent service. Directory identity follows moves and renames from its first identified version; restore targets its current location.

Run pnpm dev:web to start the Web UI and local service at http://localhost:7200. Build with pnpm build:web and serve the production UI and API with pnpm start:web. The Web application uses filesystem workspaces and supports directory selection, Git remote sync, shared Agent tools and bundled-content updates. Development, production and tests use separate data directories.

Use Settings → Data and maintenance → Migrate browser data to back up and import existing IndexedDB workspaces, including files, resources, Skills, sessions, trash and Git history. After a successful validated import, the source IndexedDB records are cleared and the complete backup is retained. Failed imports and changed source records are kept. Detection requires the original browser origin; importing a backup file does not clear current browser data.

Feature completion requires repository-wide ESLint and Prettier checks plus relevant unit and end-to-end tests. Pull requests run the full validation suite. Every product or standalone package release reviews the Agent tooling, user authoring recommendations, and system introduction; the introduction must receive a substantive prose update each time.
User authoring recommendations provide advice and examples. They are maintained independently from executable Agent defaults and never become default Agent instructions.
